items.label: Geographic Focus
items.text: Kilifi County and Tana River County

problemStatement.heading: One of Kenya's Most Important Fishing Grounds Is Under Threat
problemStatement.text: The Malindi-Ungwana Bay, shared by Kilifi and Tana River Counties, supports both artisanal and industrial fisheries. However, the area faces severe resource decline driven by illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing and destructive trawling, which persist despite legal restrictions on nearshore trawling.

cards.title: Malindi-Ungwana Bay
cards.text: Weak enforcement has led to industrial encroachment into artisanal fishing zones, resulting in habitat degradation, gear loss, and conflicts, while seagrass and nursery habitats continue to deteriorate.

cards.title: Kilifi County
cards.text: Small-scale fisheries remain the foundation of coastal livelihoods but are under increasing pressure from overfishing and destructive gear use. Encouragingly, successful BMU-led initiatives such as in Kuruwitu demonstrate that empowered BMUs can restore fish stocks and habitats.

cards.title: Tana River County
cards.text: Diverse estuarine and deltaic fisheries are similarly threatened by illegal trawling, unsustainable practices, and upstream land-use changes, while the local BMU Network remains institutionally weak.

objectives.heading: A Timely and Strategic Intervention
objectives.text: The initiative supports an advocacy campaign of the Indian Ocean Water Body, alongside the Kilifi and Tana River Beach Management Unit (BMU) Networks, implemented in partnership with Oceans Alive Foundation.
list: Strengthen community-led governance and advocacy against Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing, particularly destructive trawling, within the Malindi-Ungwana Bay ecosystem.
Respond directly to the governance and management priorities in Kenya's fisheries legislation, national policies, and the recently approved Joint Co-Management Area (JCMA) Plans.
Consolidate the gains made with the Kilifi BMU Network and extend similar capacity-building efforts to the Tana River BMU Network and the broader Indian Ocean Water Body platform.
Create a more unified and influential community-led voice capable of addressing IUU fishing and destructive trawling, and promoting sustainable fisheries governance.

jcma.heading: Backed by the Malindi-Magarini and Tana-Delta JCMA Plans
jcma.statLabel: of marine waters covered by the JCMA Plans (2024 to 2028)
jcma.text: The Malindi-Magarini and Tana-Delta JCMA Plans (2024 to 2028), which together cover over 3,100 km² of marine waters within the Malindi-Ungwana Bay, identify IUU fishing and unregulated trawling as the most significant threats to the sustainability of local fisheries.

whyOceansAlive.heading: Four Years Alongside the Kilifi BMU Network
whyOceansAlive.text: Oceans Alive Foundation, which has been actively supporting the Kilifi BMU Network over the past four years, is well positioned to lead this initiative. The organisation has demonstrated experience in:
items: Building institutional capacity for coordination and accountability
Promoting awareness and information sharing among BMU members and stakeholders
Supporting enabling policy and legislative environments for sustainable fisheries management at county level

conclusion.text: "By empowering these networks, the project will create a more unified and influential community-led voice capable of addressing IUU fishing and destructive trawling, promoting sustainable fisheries governance, and contributing to the long-term ecological and economic resilience of the Malindi-Ungwana Bay."

callToAction.heading: Help Amplify Coastal Voices
callToAction.text: Your support helps fisherfolk communities in Kilifi and Tana River stand together against illegal fishing and destructive trawling.
